newsitem.title: INDIA: Monsoon rains hit southern Indian states.
newsitem.headline: Monsoon rains hit southern Indian states.

text.p: India's southwest monsoon has struck the southern state of Kerala after being delayed by more than a week, a senior Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) official said on Tuesday.
"Monsoon has set over Kerala yesterday," A.V.R. Krishna Rao, a senior IMD official told Reuters. "It has also set in over Tamil Nadu and parts of the northeastern states."
Rao said monsoon rains were expected to cover more areas in the eastern states on Tuesday.
The monsoon rains usually start around June 1 and move progressively north, eventually covering the entire country before tapering off in September.
IMD has forecast a normal monsoon for the 10th sucessive year.
Last week IMD officials said the monsoon rains were delayed due to the influence of the middle latitude system over the Indian region.
During the four months of southwest monsoon season, June to September, India receives on an average about 88 cm of rainfall, which amounts to 80 percent of its annual rainfall.
